question.text: An applicant incorporated or established in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) is deemed to be:

answer.text: Ineligible for FPI registration in India
Appropriately regulated for FPI registration purposes
Required to obtain separate SEBI registration before FPI application
Eligible only for Category-II FPI registration

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 200 directly supports that under the SEBI (FPI) Regulations an applicant incorporated or established in an International Financial Services Centre is deemed to be appropriately regulated, so it need not separately demonstrate regulatory compliance from its home jurisdiction. The Trap: The other options understate the IFSC dispensation: IFSC-based applicants are not ineligible, do not need a separate prior SEBI registration before applying as FPIs, and are not restricted to Category-II only. Note: Pages 196 and 198 also support IFSC-related relaxations to NRI/OCI/RI contribution limits available to IFSC entities under the FPI framework.
